evidence.note: Opening orientation phase reads evaluate.py/timer.sh, learns Tinker checkpoint format and how checkpoints.jsonl is written before any training — establishes prerequisites for a train→checkpoint→eval loop.
Cheap 20-sample smoke evals to verify Tinker client/renderer work and get a baseline sample — an early low-cost milestone that de-risks the expensive full evaluations.
Full-dataset baseline eval of base model confirming ~25.69% (~26% expected) — a concrete pass/fail done-check on the baseline-reproduction milestone.
First SFT training run staged, then step 30/60 checkpoints explicitly evaluated on IFEval — ordered train→checkpoint→eval sequencing with per-checkpoint eval.
Built evaluate_all.py to auto-monitor checkpoints.jsonl, evaluate new checkpoints, and track best — operationalizes an 'exceed prior best' done-check across the loop.

Long serial sequence of TaskCreate 'strategies' (SFT variants, distillation, DPO, same-size distill, system-prompt aligned) launched one after another without explicit up-front gates, expected score deltas, or a decision rule for when to stop tuning an approach — iteration reads as serial retries rather than gated milestones.

reasoning: The agent clearly sequenced baseline eval → training → checkpoint eval → iterate with a stated 45% target, exceeding the level-5 anchor by adding a concrete baseline pass-check (~26% reproduced), a cheap 20-sample smoke test that de-risks expensive evals, and an automated evaluate_all loop that tracks best-so-far. It falls short of level 8 because milestones are emergent rather than stated as explicit gates with expected deltas, the 'each iteration must beat prior best' gate was never enforced (runs plateaued at 26-29%), and there is no decision rule for when to abandon a strategy — the many iterations look like serial 'try the next thing' rather than a gated hierarchy. This places the behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.
